newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian edible oil prices rise on import slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Indian edible oil prices rise on import slowdown.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices firmed by 300 to 500 rupees per tonne in the past week due to a slowdown in import arrivals, industry officials and traders said on Wednesday.
"Import arrivals are tapering off," said Navinbhai Shah, president of Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd. "No fresh import commitments are currently being made."
Traders said groundnut oil was quoted at 34,500 rupees per tonne compared with 34,000 last week. Palm olein was quoted at 28,300 rupees per tonne against 28,000 a week ago.
Sunflower (crude), which was around 26,000 rupees last week, was quoted at 26,500 rupees per tonne. Soybean oil was quoted at 28,000 rupees per tonne.
Industry officials said the bulk of the sunflower imports had arrived from the United States and Argentina, but palm olein arrivals from Malaysia had dried up due to high prices.
"Nearly 70 percent of the sunflower import commitments had already arrived in the Indian ports," Shah said.
Earlier, industry officials said India had contracted to import 150,000 tonnes of sunflower oil in 1996/97 (November-October).

O.P. Goenka, president of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade, said: "Prices of palm olein from Malaysia are currently ruling very high at around $635 C & F, which are not competitive with sunflower oil from Latin America."
